name: 07-evidence
title: Scientific Evidence & Acceptance — from simulation runs to reproducible claims
question:
Can the Workbench turn simulation outputs into traceable evidence, evaluate explicit
acceptance criteria, tell supported claims from unsupported ones, and flag the
verification still needed?
objective:
Show the evidence-and-acceptance method end to end. Take the study-05 engine-vs-SBML
comparison, declare acceptance criteria with tolerances up front, evaluate them
against the committed evidence, and link each verdict to its artifact — producing at
least one pass, one fail, and one pending criterion.
claim:
The Workbench evaluates pre-declared acceptance criteria against committed evidence
and records a traceable verdict for each. Using the study-05 severe-arm milestones as
the evidence source (evaluate_acceptance.py -> out/acceptance_eval.json), four criteria
were declared with tolerances and evaluated: INFLAM-01 (minimum tissue integrity agrees
to within 1%) passes at 0.0044% relative error; INFLAM-02 (peak blood pathogen within
1%) passes at 0.12%; HEMO-01 (time to MAP < 65 mmHg agrees within 6 h) fails at 15.3 h
apart (engine 69.3 h vs SBML 54.1 h); and SURR-01 (surrogate hemodynamic accuracy within
10% of the exact engine) is pending — its validator has not been run. Two pass, one fail,
one pending, each linked to its evidence artifact or its missing-evidence note.

expected_behavior.name: pass-fail-pending-acceptance-criteria
expected_behavior.statement: At least one passing, one failing, and one pending acceptance criterion are produced, each linked to a concrete evidence artifact or a clearly named missing test.

expected_behavior.name: verdicts-trace-to-evidence
expected_behavior.statement: Each criterion declares its tolerance before evaluation and records the measured value and the artifact it came from, so the verdict is reproducible from committed data.

findings.summary: Four pre-declared criteria evaluate to 2 pass, 1 fail, 1 pending — each traced to evidence (see chart 01).
findings.detail:
evaluate_acceptance.py reads the committed study-05 milestones
(02-ensembles/data/{engine,sbml}-sev3.milestones.json), applies each criterion's
declared tolerance, and writes out/acceptance_eval.json:
  * INFLAM-01 pass — minimum tissue integrity: engine 0.243052 vs SBML 0.243042,
    relative error 0.0044% (tolerance 1%).
  * INFLAM-02 pass — peak blood pathogen: engine 330.20 vs SBML 330.60,
    relative error 0.12% (tolerance 1%).
  * HEMO-01 fail — time to MAP < 65 mmHg: engine 69.3 h vs SBML 54.1 h, 15.3 h
    apart (tolerance 6 h). This is the known hemodynamic divergence from study 05,
    now expressed as a failed, evidence-linked acceptance criterion.
  * SURR-01 pending — surrogate hemodynamic accuracy within 10% of the exact engine:
    the criterion is declared, but the held-out surrogate-vs-exact validator has not
    been run, so it is reported pending, not passed.
The split is the point: the inflammation core passes, the hemodynamic layer fails,
and the surrogate's clinical accuracy is an open verification need. Each verdict
links back to the exact artifact (or names the missing test), so the claims are
traceable rather than asserted.

findings.summary: The study's scientific verdict is reconciled with its pending acceptance metadata, not quietly rewritten.
findings.detail:
This study's own verdict is 'supported' for one specific claim: the acceptance
machinery runs and produces linked pass/fail/pending verdicts. That is separate
from the scientific status of the sepsis model itself, which the gates report
honestly — the hemodynamic criterion fails and the surrogate criterion is pending.
A completed demonstration verdict and an open acceptance gate coexist here on
purpose: the Workbench records the pending gate rather than inflating the verdict to
mask it.
findings.statement: Study 07 demonstrates the acceptance method, not a clean bill of health for the sepsis model.
findings.explanation: The supported verdict is scoped to the method: committed evidence flows through declared criteria to traceable pass/fail/pending verdicts, with at least one of each, each linked to an artifact or a named missing test. It does not claim the sepsis model passes overall. Two of its gates do not: HEMO-01 fails (the hemodynamic divergence from study 05) and SURR-01 is pending (the surrogate accuracy validator is unrun). Reporting those honestly, beside a completed demonstration verdict, is the behavior the study is meant to show. The follow-up that would close SURR-01 is a held-out, multi-seed surrogate-vs-exact trajectory comparison (study 04); the follow-up that would turn HEMO-01 into an explained result rather than a bare failure is the mechanistic perturbation test (study 05).
